summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis was admitted for severe joint pain following a gastrointestinal flare, unresponsive to oral steroids and pain medications. He was treated with IV methylprednisolone and IV analgesics, with successful transition to oral prednisone and home pain regimen as symptoms improved. MRI showed mild tenosynovitis without erosions, confirming active inflammatory arthritis. His diabetes and hypertension were managed with home medications. He was discharged home on a prednisone taper with instructions to follow up with rheumatology.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
